newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close stronger amid currency gains.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close stronger amid currency gains.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Monday, outperforming U.S. treasuries, as gains in the U.S. bond market and a jump in the the Canadian dollar boosted prices, analysts said.

"We've seen some buying of the U.S. currency and U.S. bonds and I think some of that has spilled over into the Canadian market as well," said Jim Webber, director of fixed-income research TD Securities Inc. "It's a sort of flight to North America."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond rose C$0.75 to C$107.25 to yield 7.370 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond rose 17/32 to yield 7.08 percent. The spread between the two bonds narrowed to 29 basis points from 31 basis points at the close of trading on Friday.

Canadian and U.S. bond rallied this morning as the U.S. dollar rose to a 50-month high against the yen. The strength in the U.S. dollar reflected positively on Canadian markets and helped the Canadian dollar strengthen off the two-year low against the U.S. dollar it reached on Friday.
But analysts said that gains could be short-lived and would depend partly on the strength of U.S. economic reports due out later this week.

"I don't know how long this can last. We do have some fairly significant U.S. numbers coming out toward the end of the week," said Webber. Among the reports are the U.S. producer price index and retail sales report for March.

In economic news, the value of Canadian building permits issued in February rose 4.7 percent to C$2.537 billion, seasonally adjusted, from January. Economists surveyed by Reuters had forecast on average a month-on-month rise of 2.3 percent.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 10-year benchmark bond rose C$0.77 to C$101.22 to yield 6.823 percent.

The U.S. bond rose 9/32 to yield 6.86 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to a negative spread of four basis points from a positive spread of two basis points at the close of trading on Friday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 3.14 percent against its U.S. equivalent, which yielded 5.28 percent.
